one_line: Regulators clamp down, investors pour billions, and firms tighten AI safety.

themes.title: Regulators target AI firms and chips
themes.text: California Attorney General sued OpenAI over a cyberattack, while the U.S. Commerce Department and DOJ investigated a Singapore chip reseller and announced new export licenses for AI chips to Southeast Asian data centers. Nvidia’s board also created a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee and its former CEO will testify before House committees.

stories.headline: California AG Rob Bonta sues OpenAI over Hugging Face incident
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify before US House committees on Dec 1
US Commerce Dept and DOJ investigated Megaspeed over chip exports in 2024
US tightens AI chip export rules, targeting Southeast Asia data centres
Nvidia board creates National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee

themes.title: Billion‑dollar funding pours into AI startups
themes.text: Altimeter Capital plans a $5 billion investment in Anthropic’s IPO, Alphabet’s Isomorphic Labs secured a $5 billion Series C to accelerate AI‑driven drug trials, and Paris‑based Genesis AI raised $500 million Series A at a $3.5 billion valuation for robot production and infrastructure.

stories.headline: Altimeter aims to invest $5B in Anthropic IPO
Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion Series C to speed AI‑driven drug trials
Genesis AI raises $500 million Series A at $3.5 billion valuation

themes.title: AI safety steps tighten disclosure and testing
themes.text: Anthropic reduced its coordinated vulnerability disclosure window to 30 days for serious flaws, and OpenAI signed agreements with four independent evaluators to run pilot safety assessments of its models.

stories.headline: Anthropic cuts vulnerability disclosure window to 30 days for serious flaws
OpenAI partners with independent evaluators for safety pilots
